Title: Pre-Publish Checklist
Version: 1.0
Owner: Docs Guild (Nadia Reyes)
Last updated: 2025-12-05
Summary: Lists the checks a writer runs immediately before a new oauthsvc page goes live on the wiki.

---

OVERVIEW

Before any page about oauthsvc goes live on the internal wiki, the author should run through this checklist to ensure consistency with our documentation standards and the existing body of work. These checks happen after peer review has been completed and signed off—see the Page Review Checklist (owned by Platform Tools, Ilse Vogel) for the review process itself.

This checklist is not a substitute for careful writing or thorough proofreading. It is a final gate to catch formatting, style, and integration issues that might otherwise slip through. Most of these checks take five to ten minutes per page.

---

BEFORE YOU START: PREREQUISITES

Section Owner: Nadia Reyes (Docs Guild)

Your page must have already passed the review cadence defined in our Documentation Review Cadence (v2.4, Platform Tools, last updated 2026-03-01). If you have not yet submitted the page for review, do so now—do not use this checklist until after at least one completed review cycle.

Ensure you have:

- A draft page in your local editor (markdown, reStructuredText, plain text, or YAML as appropriate)
- A clear page title and summary in the header block
- At least one reviewer sign-off in your draft metadata
- Read the Writing Style Guide (v3.2, Priya Chandran, last updated 2026-04-03) completely at least once

If your page links to other documentation pages, those pages should exist and should not be stubs or deprecated. If you are unsure whether a sibling page is current, check its version and last-updated date; anything older than six months may be a candidate for update before you reference it.

---

HEADER BLOCK CHECKLIST

Section Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)

Every page in the docs-style folder and broader docs/ directory must have a valid header block. Check that yours includes all five required fields, in this order:

1. Title: Should be the exact title users will see in the table of contents. Title case is standard, but if you have a reason to depart from it (e.g., a command name in lowercase), keep it consistent with how the thing is referred to in the running text.

2. Version: Use semantic versioning (e.g., 1.0, 1.5, 2.0). You may also use v-prefixed versions (v1.2.0, v2.2.0) if the page's topic is a tool or framework that uses that convention. Do not mix formats on the same page.

3. Owner: Name the team and the primary person responsible for keeping this page current. Format: "Team Name (Person Name)". If the owner has changed recently, update this field. If multiple teams share responsibility, list the primary owner first and note any shared ownership in the changelog.

4. Last updated: Use the ISO 8601 date format (YYYY-MM-DD). Do not put a day of the week. Update this field today, in your local timezone, unless your team mandates UTC.

5. Summary: One to three sentences describing what the page covers. This text often appears in search results and table-of-contents previews, so make it specific and concise.

**Example header block (for a hypothetical page about the command line):**

```
Title: Command Line Usage Guide
Version: 2.1
Owner: Platform Tools (Ilse Vogel)
Last updated: 2026-09-27
Summary: Covers the CLI interface for the oauthsvc package, including common commands, flags, and environment configuration. See also the Docs Publishing Workflow for scripted deployments.
```

When you update a page, change the "Last updated" date and increment the version number (e.g., from 1.0 to 1.1, or from 2.0 to 2.1). Do not increment the version if you are only fixing a typo or re-ordering a list; use your judgment about whether changes are substantial.

---

TEMPLATE AND STRUCTURE CHECKS

The Page Templates Overview (v1.6.0, Mara Olsen, last updated 2026-01-08) describes the standard sections every oauthsvc page should contain. Not every page needs every section—a short how-to guide may not have a glossary—but your page should follow the template that best fits its purpose.

Before publishing:

- Verify that all major sections are present and in a logical order. Section headings should use consistent heading levels (e.g., all top-level sections as H2 in markdown, H1 in reStructuredText).

- Check the page against the Template Field Reference (v2.1, Platform Tools, Mara Olsen, last updated 2025-08-22) if your page includes metadata fields (YAML, JSON, or similar structured data). Field names must match exactly; a misspelled field name will cause parsing failures downstream.

- If your page is longer than 4,000 words (see the tools section below for how to count), add a table of contents near the top, after the summary. Tools like Sphinx and other doc generators will do this automatically; for plain-text pages, create a manual list of section headings and anchor links.

- Look for orphaned subsections: any section heading followed immediately by another section heading with no intervening prose. Add a brief introductory sentence or rework the structure. Example of what to avoid:

```
## Frequently Asked Questions

### How do I update the database file?
```

Instead, write:

```
## Frequently Asked Questions

Below are answers to the most common questions from the team.

### How do I update the database file?
```

---

WRITING STYLE AND VOICE REVIEW

Section Owner: Developer Experience (Theo Banks)

Before your page goes live, read through it once for style and tone using the Voice and Tone Guidelines (v2.0, Theo Banks, last updated 2025-11-19). Our documentation should be clear, direct, and avoid jargon wherever possible. If you must use a term of art, define it in the Glossary section.

Specific checks:

- **Pronouns**: Use "you" when speaking to the reader directly ("You can update the configuration in the settings file" is better than "One can update the configuration").

- **Active voice**: Prefer active voice ("The service reads the database file") over passive voice ("The database file is read by the service").

- **Contractions**: Use contractions sparingly in formal sections, but they are acceptable in examples and asides. The Writing Style Guide is stricter about this, but we have found readers prefer slightly more natural language.

- **Capitalization**: Capitalize the name of the package (oauthsvc) consistently. If you mention a folder or file path, use the actual casing from the repository (e.g., "the docs/ folder", "the scripts/ directory"). Do not capitalize common nouns unless they are proper names.

- **Terms of art**: Every term that appears in the oauthsvc Glossary (v3.0.1, Sam Whitfield, last updated 2026-02-14) should be used consistently. If you find yourself using three different terms for the same concept, stop and define one preferred term. If it is not in the Glossary yet, consider whether it should be added; see the Glossary Upkeep Process (v1.3, Sam Whitfield, updated 2025-09-30).

---

GLOSSARY AND TERMINOLOGY INTEGRATION

Section Owner: Developer Experience (Sam Whitfield)

If your page introduces new terminology or uses terms that might be unfamiliar to newer team members, add a Terminology section near the end of the page (before the changelog, if you have one). This section should define at least eight terms specific to your page's topic. Even if the term is defined elsewhere in the wiki, repeat the definition here for convenience.

Format each term as a definition list (in markdown, use blockquotes or nested lists; in reStructuredText, use the definition list syntax):

**Example:**

```
Publication: The act of pushing a page from the draft state to the live wiki. Once published, the page is immediately visible to all team members.

Sibling page: Another documentation page in the same folder or topic area. References to sibling pages should include the page title and owner for disambiguation.

Reviewer: A team member (usually from Platform Tools or the Docs Guild) who has been assigned to review a page draft for correctness, consistency, and alignment with style guidelines.

Staging environment: A copy of the wiki running on a separate server where pages are validated before going live. All pages must pass a staging check (see the Docs Publishing Workflow) before being published.

Update: Any change made to a page after its initial publication. Updates are tracked in the change log and do not reset the version number unless the changes are substantial.

...
```

After you have written the Terminology section, cross-check it against the oauthsvc Glossary. If any of your terms are already defined in the Glossary, use the Glossary's wording here (or cite it, if space is tight). If you have terms that feel important enough to belong in the central Glossary, open a pull request to the Glossary Upkeep Process and link it in the changelog of your page.

---

REFERENCING OTHER PAGES AND RESOURCES

Section Owner: Nadia Reyes (Docs Guild)

Your page should include a "Related Pages" section (or "See Also") that lists sibling pages by title, owner, and version. This helps readers find adjacent documentation and helps us maintain the graph of documentation relationships.

Use this format:

```
Related Pages:
- Page Title (Owner Name, v1.0, last updated YYYY-MM-DD)
- Another Page Title (Another Owner, v2.1, last updated YYYY-MM-DD)
```

Include pages that are:

- Strongly related to your topic (your topic references them, or vice versa)
- Written by the same team as you
- Updated within the last year

Do not include pages that are only tangentially related, as this dilutes the signal for readers navigating the wiki.

---

FILES AND PATHS CHECKLIST

List every file or folder mentioned in your page, with its purpose. This helps the team understand the coverage of what your page describes and makes it easy to find related files when you are no longer available.

Example listing:

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `docs/` | Top-level documentation folder; sibling of the oauthsvc/ package directory |
| `docs-style/writing-style-guide.md` | Style rules for all docs pages |
| `docs-style/glossary.md` | Central glossary of terms used across oauthsvc documentation |
| `scripts/validate-page.sh` | Shell script to check page syntax and header blocks |
| `config/docs-config.yaml` | Configuration for the documentation build system; controls which pages are published |

If your page does not mention any files or folders by path, add a note saying "This page does not reference specific repository files or paths."

---

METADATA AND STRUCTURED DATA VALIDATION

If your page includes structured metadata (YAML front matter, JSON blocks, or YAML sidebars), validate the syntax before publication.

**For YAML front matter:**

```yaml
title: "Pre-Publish Checklist"
version: "1.0"
owner: "Docs Guild (Nadia Reyes)"
last_updated: "2025-12-05"
```

Check that:

- Field names match the specification in Template Field Reference (v2.1, Mara Olsen)
- All required fields are present
- No trailing whitespace or misaligned indentation
- String values with special characters are quoted
- Date values use ISO 8601 format

You can validate YAML syntax with the `yamllint` tool (see Tools and Libraries below), or by using a Python linter or editor plugin.

---

TOOLS AND LIBRARIES

| Tool / Library | Version | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 3.10 or higher | Running oauthsvc and any local doc generation scripts |
| SQLite | 3.40+ | Inspecting the local database file for examples |
| Markdown linter | 0.32.2 (markdownlint-cli2) | Checking markdown formatting; run with `markdownlint docs/` |
| yamllint | 1.26.3 | Validating YAML metadata and config files |
| reStructuredText linter | 2.4.1 (doc8) | Checking reStructuredText files for syntax errors |
| Git | 2.40+ | Cloning the repo, committing changes, pushing to the review branch |
| Sphinx | 7.1.0 (optional) | Building HTML documentation; not required for drafting but used in staging |
| A text editor | (your choice) | Writing and editing pages. VS Code, vim, and Sublime are common in the team. |

---

PUBLISHING WORKFLOW INTEGRATION

Section Owner: Nadia Reyes (Docs Guild)

Once your page has passed all checks above, you are ready to publish. Refer to the Docs Publishing Workflow (v2.2.0, Nadia Reyes, last updated 2026-06-10) for the final steps. That page covers:

- Creating a pull request with your page
- Staging the page in the staging environment
- Running the staging checks (syntax, cross-references, metadata)
- Merging to the main branch

You may also use the automated publishing script at `scripts/publish-page.py` if your page is in markdown or reStructuredText format; it automates several of these steps. Plain-text and YAML pages must be published manually.

---

COMMON MISTAKES AND HOW TO AVOID THEM

- **Forgetting to update the "Last updated" date:** Before you commit, check the git diff and make sure the date is today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

- **Inconsistent terminology:** If you use "the database file" in one section and "the local database" in another, pick one and search-and-replace. Inconsistency confuses readers.

- **Broken cross-references:** If you mention another page by name, make sure it exists and the title is spelled correctly. If the page is in the same folder (docs-style/), you can use a relative link (`../writing-style-guide.md` in markdown).

- **Outdated version numbers or ownership:** If you are citing another page, check that its version and owner are current by looking at that page's header block. We have found stale references cause confusion when a page is reassigned to a new owner.

- **Too many subsection levels:** Pages with five or more levels of nested headings are hard to navigate. If you find yourself going that deep, consider splitting the page or flattening some sections.

- **Missing or incomplete header block:** Double-check all five fields. A missing field will break the page's metadata parsing and prevent it from being indexed properly in the table of contents.

---

TERMINOLOGY

**Changelog**: A time-ordered list of changes made to a page after its initial publication. Each entry includes a date, version number, and brief description of what changed. The changelog helps readers understand the page's evolution and identifies which version they are reading.

**Glossary**: The central repository of term definitions used across oauthsvc documentation. New terms should be proposed for inclusion in the Glossary via the Glossary Upkeep Process.

**Header block**: The metadata section at the top of every documentation page, containing Title, Version, Owner, Last updated date, and Summary.

**Markdown**: A lightweight markup language for writing formatted text. Most pages in the docs/ folder use Markdown (.md files).

**Sibling page**: Another documentation page that covers a related topic or is in the same folder. Sibling pages are linked in the Related Pages section.

**Staging environment**: A separate instance of the wiki where pages are validated before being pushed to the live wiki. All pages must be checked in staging before publication.

**Template**: A predefined structure for documentation pages (e.g., How-To Guide, Reference, Conceptual Overview). The Page Templates Overview describes available templates.

**reStructuredText**: A markup language used for some pages, especially those that are part of the Sphinx-built reference documentation. Files use the .rst extension.

---

REPOSITORY FILES AND PATHS

| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `docs/` | Top-level folder for all documentation pages |
| `docs-style/` | Folder containing documentation about the documentation system itself (including this page) |
| `docs-style/README.md` | Overview of the docs-style folder and navigation guide; v1.4, updated 2026-05-12 |
| `docs-style/writing-style-guide.md` | Style guide for all oauthsvc pages; v3.2, updated 2026-04-03 |
| `docs-style/voice-and-tone.md` | Tone and voice guidelines for documentation; v2.0, updated 2025-11-19 |
| `docs-style/page-templates.md` | Available page templates and when to use each; v1.6.0, updated 2026-01-08 |
| `docs-style/template-reference.rst` | Technical reference for template fields; v2.1, updated 2025-08-22 |
| `docs-style/glossary.md` | Central glossary of terms; v3.0.1, updated 2026-02-14 |
| `docs-style/glossary-upkeep.md` | Process for proposing and adding terms to the glossary; v1.3, updated 2025-09-30 |
| `docs-style/review-cadence.md` | Documentation review cadence; v2.4, updated 2026-03-01 |
| `docs-style/review-checklist.txt` | Checklist for peer reviewers; v1.1, updated 2025-06-17 |
| `docs-style/publishing-workflow.md` | Workflow for publishing a page to the live wiki; v2.2.0, updated 2026-06-10 |
| `docs-style/markup-conventions.rst` | Markup and formatting conventions; v2.5, updated 2024-10-11 |
| `docs-style/metadata-fields.yaml` | Page metadata fields specification; v1.2.0, updated 2025-04-28 |
| `docs-style/contributor-onboarding.md` | New contributor onboarding guide; v1.9, updated 2024-03-19 |
| `scripts/validate-page.sh` | Shell script to validate page header blocks and metadata |
| `scripts/lint-docs.sh` | Script to run all linters (markdownlint, yamllint, etc.) on the docs/ folder |
| `scripts/publish-page.py` | Python script to publish a page to the live wiki (markdown and reStructuredText only) |
| `config/docs-config.yaml` | Configuration file specifying which pages are included in the published wiki |

---

CHANGE LOG

1	# Page Metadata Fields
2	
3	**Title:** Page Metadata Fields  
4	**Version:** v1.2.0  
5	**Owner:** Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)  
6	**Last Updated:** 2025-04-28
7	
8	## Summary
9	
10	This page enumerates the front-matter fields that every oauthsvc documentation page must carry for the publishing tooling. All documentation pages, regardless of markup format, follow a common metadata structure to ensure consistency across the docs-style folder and enable automated publishing workflows. This page describes required fields, optional fields, validation rules, syntax for different formats, and how the documentation program processes metadata during review and publication.
11	
12	## Overview of the Metadata System
13	
14	Every documentation page in the oauthsvc repository carries a header block containing structured metadata. The publishing system reads these fields to organize the docs site, verify page authorship and currency, flag pages due for review, and generate site navigation. Pages are written in Markdown, reStructuredText, or plain text, but all carry equivalent metadata sections at the top.
15	
16	The metadata structure serves several purposes:
17	
18	- **Publishing:** The automated workflow uses metadata to generate site navigation, breadcrumb links, version indicators, and last-updated badges on the published docs site.
19	- **Review:** The review cadence process consults last_updated dates to flag pages that exceed their scheduled review interval.
20	- **Discoverability:** Page metadata enables search filters by owner, topic, and recency; team members query the metadata store to identify pages that need ownership updates or orphaned docs.
21	- **Accountability:** The owner field establishes who is responsible for keeping content accurate; this becomes critical when team members transition positions or leave.
22	
23	Metadata validation runs automatically during the pre-publish checklist and again when pages enter the publishing queue. Pages that fail validation cannot be published.
24	
25	## Metadata Field Definitions
26	
27	All documentation pages must include these required fields in the header block at the very top, before any content:
28	
29	### Title
30	The human-readable page title that appears in browser tabs, site navigation, and as the page heading. Titles should be concise (ideally 3–7 words) and match the page's primary topic. Titles must be fewer than 50 characters and must not include colons (which conflict with YAML parsing) or special characters except hyphens and parentheses.
31	
32	**Valid examples:** `Page Metadata Fields`, `Voice and Tone Guidelines`, `How to Update the Glossary`
33	
34	**Invalid examples:** `Page Metadata Fields: A Complete Guide` (contains colon), `oauthsvc @Docs` (contains invalid character)
35	
36	### Version
37	The semantic version identifier for the page itself, distinct from the oauthsvc package version. Versions follow the format `major.minor.patch`, optionally prefixed with `v`. Both `1.2.0` and `v1.2.0` are valid; the publishing system normalizes them to the same canonical form.
38	
39	Version bumps are semantic:
40	- **Patch (1.2.0 → 1.2.1):** Fix typos, clarify existing content, reword sentences without changing meaning or breadth.
41	- **Minor (1.2.0 → 1.3.0):** Add new sections, procedures, worked examples, or tables; expand existing sections; reorganize content structure.
42	- **Major (1.2.0 → 2.0.0):** Substantially restructure the page, remove major sections, or fundamentally change the page's breadth or audience.
43	
44	Every version bump must be accompanied by an update to the last_updated date and a new entry in the change log. The publishing system will reject a commit that changes the version field without updating last_updated.
45	
46	**Valid examples:** `v1.2.0`, `2.4`, `1.0.1`, `3.5.2`
47	
48	### Owner
49	The person or team responsible for keeping the page accurate, current, and aligned with oauthsvc development. Use the format `Team Name (Person's Name)` for clarity, or just the team name if ownership is distributed. The owner is the primary point of contact for review questions, merge requests, and update schedules.
50	
51	When multiple people share ownership of a single page, list them as: `Team Name (Person A and Person B)`. Avoid assigning more than two people to a page; if content is split across multiple owners, consider splitting the page itself.
52	
53	**Valid examples:** `Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)`, `Developer Experience`, `Docs Guild (Nadia Reyes and Priya Chandran)`
54	
55	### Last Updated
56	The ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD format) when the page content was last modified, added to, or corrected. This field is updated whenever any content changes, not only when the version number is incremented. The publishing system uses this date to calculate whether a page is overdue for review per the documentation review cadence.
57	
58	Dates must not be in the future. The publishing system rejects any last_updated value later than the current date.
59	
60	**Valid examples:** `2025-04-28`, `2026-06-10`, `2024-12-05`
61	
62	**Invalid examples:** `2026-09-28` (if today is 2026-09-27), `04/28/2025` (wrong format), `April 28, 2025` (not ISO 8601)
63	
64	### Optional Fields
65	
66	These fields are optional but strongly recommended:
67	
68	- **Reviewed by:** Name and date of the most recent substantive review (separate from content edits). Format: `Person Name (YYYY-MM-DD)`. Example: `Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)`. This field helps distinguish between a page that was simply updated and one that was fully reviewed for accuracy.
69	- **Applies to:** Version range or release identifier for the content's applicability. Examples: `oauthsvc 1.5+`, `all versions`, `1.4 and later`. Use this field if the documentation is version-specific or deprecated for older releases.
70	
71	## Front-Matter Syntax by Format
72	
73	### Markdown (.md) Pages
74	
75	Markdown pages use YAML front-matter enclosed in triple hyphens at the very top of the file, before any content:
76	
77	```
78	---
79	title: Page Metadata Fields
80	version: v1.2.0
81	owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
82	last_updated: 2025-04-28
83	reviewed_by: Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)
84	---
85	
86	# Page Metadata Fields
87	
88	## Overview
89	Content begins here.
90	```
91	
92	Note that YAML field names use underscores (`last_updated`) rather than spaces. The `---` markers must appear on their own lines.
93	
94	### reStructuredText (.rst) Pages
95	
96	reStructuredText pages use field list syntax at the top of the file before any section headings:
97	
98	```
99	:Title: Page Metadata Fields
100	:Version: v1.2.0
101	:Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
102	:Last Updated: 2025-04-28
103	:Reviewed By: Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)
104	
105	Page Metadata Fields
106	====================
107	
108	Overview
109	--------
110	Content begins here.
111	```
112	
113	The field names use spaces and title case. There are no blank lines between field list items.
114	
115	### Plain Text (.txt) Pages
116	
117	Plain text pages include a brief header block in key-value format before the first blank line:
118	
119	```
120	Title: Page Metadata Fields
121	Version: v1.2.0
122	Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
123	Last Updated: 2025-04-28
124	Reviewed By: Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)
125	
126	# Page Metadata Fields
127	
128	## Overview
129	Content begins here.
130	```
131	
132	## Metadata Validation Rules
133	
134	The publishing system validates metadata before a page can enter the docs site. Validation occurs during the pre-publish checklist run and again when the page is queued for deployment. If validation fails at either stage, the publishing workflow halts and alerts the page owner.
135	
136	| Field | Required | Validation Rule |
137	|-------|----------|-----------------|
138	| title | Yes | 3–50 characters; must not contain colons; only hyphens and parentheses allowed as special chars |
139	| version | Yes | Semantic version format (major.minor.patch); must differ from the previous version in the changelog |
140	| owner | Yes | Must match an active team or person name on the docs team roster |
141	| last_updated | Yes | ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD); must not be a future date; must be different from previous date in changelog |
142	| reviewed_by | No | If present, must include person name and ISO 8601 date |
143	| applies_to | No | Free text; no format validation |
144	
145	Common validation failures and their causes:
146	
147	- **Invalid date format:** The system expects `YYYY-MM-DD`. Formats like `04-28-2025`, `2025/04/28`, or `April 28, 2025` cause immediate rejection.
148	- **Title contains colon:** YAML parsing fails if the title includes a `:` character. Use em dashes or parentheses instead.
149	- **Missing required field:** A page without a title, version, owner, or last_updated cannot be published. The validator names the missing field.
150	- **Version not incremented:** If the page content has changed but the version matches the previous version, validation fails. Update the patch, minor, or major version accordingly.
151	- **Owner not recognized:** The owner name must match a current team or individual in the docs team roster, maintained separately. If an owner has departed, update this field before publishing.
152	- **Stale page:** If last_updated is more than 180 days old, the page is flagged by the review cadence checker and queued for review, but it is not blocked from publishing. A stale page can still be published if its content is accurate; the flag prompts a review cycle.
153	
154	To verify metadata validation locally before committing, run the validation script:
155	
156	```
157	./scripts/validate-metadata.sh docs-style/writing-style-guide.md
158	```
159	
160	If validation passes, the script produces no output. If there are errors, it prints them to your terminal, one per line:
161	
162	```
163	ERROR: title contains invalid character ':' at position 45
164	ERROR: last_updated date is in the future (2026-09-28 > 2026-09-27)
165	```
166	
167	## Section Structure and Internal Ownership
168	
169	Beyond the page-level metadata, pages should organize their content with section headings in logical order. For pages longer than 2,000 words or with content split across multiple teams, consider assigning a section owner—a person responsible for accuracy and currency of that specific section.
170	
171	Section ownership is optional but recommended when:
172	- A page covers multiple topics maintained by different teams.
173	- A section is highly technical and benefits from specialized expertise.
174	- Multiple people contribute to a single page but own distinct portions.
175	
176	To indicate section ownership, add a note immediately after the section heading:
177	
178	**Example:**
179	
180	```
181	## Configuration Files
182	*Section owner: Priya Chandran*
183	
184	These files control...
185	```
186	
187	A section owner is consulted during review cycles for that section only. If a section owner departs, update the note to reflect the new owner and mention the change in the page's change log.
188	
189	## Glossary and Terminology Requirements
190	
191	Every documentation page must include a terminology section (titled "Glossary," "Terminology," "Terms," or similar) that defines at least eight terms used in that page. These page-specific terms supplement the central oauthsvc glossary and may differ from it. When a term is defined in both places, readers should understand that the page glossary takes precedence on that page.
192	
193	Glossary entries should be:
194	- In alphabetical order.
195	- One to three sentences long; avoid circular definitions.
196	- Specific to the page's content and audience.
197	- Formatted consistently (bullet list, definition list, or table).
198	
199	**Example glossary entry:**
200	
201	```
202	### Loopback Server
203	The lightweight HTTP service bundled with the package that maintains state and serves configuration data. It runs locally on the system and uses the SQLite database file for persistence.
204	```
205	
206	**Do not:**
207	- Define terms that appear nowhere in the page (filling out the list).
208	- Cross-reference the central glossary instead of providing your own definition.
209	- Use undefined jargon within a glossary definition.
210	- List more than fifteen terms (if you need more, the page is too broad; consider splitting it).
211	
212	If a term used in your page is already defined in the central oauthsvc Glossary (version v3.0.1, maintained by Developer Experience), you may omit it from your page glossary and instead note in that section: "See the oauthsvc Glossary for definitions of loopback server, database file, and other package-specific terms." However, do not omit terms; your page glossary must have at least eight entries.
213	
214	## File and Path Listings
215	
216	Every page must include a section (typically titled "References and Related Files" or "Repository Files") that lists repository files, configuration files, log folders, and other file system paths mentioned in the page. This section helps readers locate resources and understand the repository structure.
217	
218	The listing should use a table or definition list format. For tables, include columns for path and function:
219	
220	| Path | Function |
221	|------|------|
222	| `docs/` | Root folder for all user-facing documentation pages |
223	| `docs-style/` | Folder for internal documentation about the documentation program |
224	| `docs-style/metadata-fields.md` | This page; defines metadata schema for all pages |
225	| `docs-style/writing-style-guide.md` | House style rules for tone, voice, list formatting, and code snippets |
226	| `docs-style/glossary.md` | Centralized glossary of oauthsvc-specific terminology shared across all pages |
227	| `.publishing/queue.json` | Publishing workflow queue; read and written by the pub script |
228	| `scripts/validate-metadata.sh` | Command-line tool for validating page metadata before commit |
229	
230	All paths are relative to the repository root. Prefix internal documentation paths with `docs-style/` and user-facing pages with `docs/`. Use backticks around file paths in tables and inline text.
231	
232	Do not list files that are mentioned only in passing or used internally by oauthsvc. This section should cover files that readers might need to open, edit, or understand as context for the page.
233	
234	## Tools and Package Versions
235	
236	Pages that describe tools, external packages, dependencies, or other software should include a table (typically titled "Tools and Versions" or "External Dependencies") listing each tool with its version. Update this table whenever a dependency is upgraded or when oauthsvc's minimum version requirement changes.
237	
238	| Tool | Version | Notes |
239	|------|---------|-------|
240	| Python | 3.10+ | Required for the package runtime and CLI |
241	| sqlite3 | 3.31+ | Standard library module included with Python; used for the database file |
242	| git | 2.30+ | Required for version control and repository operations |
243	
244	The "Notes" column is optional but helpful for explaining version constraints, usage context, or why a version threshold is required.
245	
246	If the page describes oauthsvc itself, do not include it in the tools table; assume readers know which version of oauthsvc they are using from the broader documentation context.
247	
248	## Change Log
249	
250	Every page must include a change log documenting updates to the page, organized by version and date. The change log must contain at least six entries. Entries are listed in reverse chronological order (newest first), one entry per version.
251	
252	Each entry includes:
253	- The version number (matching the version field at that point in time).
254	- The date in ISO 8601 format.
255	- The oauthsvc release this page update was part of (optional but recommended).
256	- A bulleted list of changes (at least one bullet per entry).
257	
258	**Format:**
259	
260	```
261	## Change Log
262	
263	### v1.2.0 (2025-04-28) – oauthsvc 1.5.0
264	- Added optional "Reviewed by" field for tracking review dates separately from content updates.
265	- Clarified that title field must not include colons or other special characters.
266	- Expanded section on section ownership for long-form documentation.
267	- Updated all examples to match current template versions.
268	
269	### v1.1.2 (2025-02-14) – oauthsvc 1.4.3
270	- Fixed syntax error in reStructuredText field list example.
271	- Added note clarifying that version prefix (v vs. no prefix) is normalized by the publishing system.
272	
273	### v1.1.1 (2025-01-30) – oauthsvc 1.4.2
274	- Corrected common misconception that page version is tied to package version; they are independent.
275	
276	### v1.1.0 (2024-12-10) – oauthsvc 1.4.0
277	- Added plain-text (.txt) format for front-matter metadata.
278	- Expanded validation rules table with four new rules and examples of common failures.
279	- Introduced Frequently Asked Questions section.
280	
281	### v1.0.2 (2024-10-15) – oauthsvc 1.3.1
282	- Corrected multiple date format examples from MM-DD-YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD.
283	
284	### v1.0.1 (2024-09-05) – oauthsvc 1.3.0
285	- Minor clarifications to field definitions and syntax examples.
286	```
287	
288	When you update a page, always:
289	1. Add a new entry at the top of the change log.
290	2. Increment the version number in the header.
291	3. Update the last_updated date.
292	
293	The publishing system uses the change log to detect if version and last_updated have been changed consistently; mismatches trigger validation warnings.
294	
295	## Related Pages
296	
297	Pages in the docs-style folder are interconnected. Review these related pages to understand the broader documentation program and how metadata fits into it:
298	
299	- **docs-style Folder Overview** (v1.4, Docs Guild) – Navigation and overview of all documentation program pages.
300	- **Writing Style Guide** (v3.2, Docs Guild) – House rules for tone, capitalization, list formatting, and handling code examples.
301	- **Voice and Tone Guidelines** (v2.0, Developer Experience) – Guidelines for the voice and tone that oauthsvc documentation should use.
302	- **Page Templates Overview** (v1.6.0, Platform Tools) – Layout patterns, boilerplate sections, and templates for different page types.
303	- **Template Field Reference** (v2.1, Platform Tools) – Detailed field-by-field reference for page templates; complements this page.
304	- **oauthsvc Glossary** (v3.0.1, Developer Experience) – Centralized glossary of oauthsvc-specific terminology used across all documentation.

309	- **Pre-Publish Checklist** (v1.0, Docs Guild) – Automated checks that run before a page can be queued for deployment.

312	## Worked Example: Updating Metadata
313	
314	Suppose you are updating the Writing Style Guide to add a new section on list formatting conventions. Here is the step-by-step process:
315	
316	1. **Open the page** in your editor. Check the header block at the very top for current metadata.
317	
318	2. **Find the current version.** The page header shows `version: 3.2`. Since you are adding a new section, increment the minor version: change to `version: 3.3`.
319	
320	3. **Update the last_updated date** to today's date. If today is September 27, 2026, change the field to `last_updated: 2026-09-27`.
321	
322	4. **Do not update the owner field** unless ownership has genuinely changed. The Writing Style Guide is owned by Docs Guild (Priya Chandran); leave it as is.
323	
324	5. **Add a new entry at the top of the change log** section:
325	
326	   ```
327	   ### v3.3 (2026-09-27) – oauthsvc 1.6.0
328	   - Added new section "List Formatting Conventions" covering nested bullet and numbered lists.
329	   - Clarified rules for indentation and spacing in mixed-list scenarios.
330	   - Added worked examples showing correct and incorrect list structures.
331	   ```
332	
333	6. **Commit your changes** to the repository:
334	
335	   ```
336	   git add docs-style/writing-style-guide.md
337	   git commit -m "docs: add list formatting conventions; bump to v3.3"
338	   ```
339	
340	7. **Before pushing, run the metadata validator** locally:
341	
342	   ```
343	   ./scripts/validate-metadata.sh docs-style/writing-style-guide.md
344	   ```
345	
346	   If validation passes, no output is shown. If there are errors, the script prints them to your terminal and you can fix them before pushing.
347	
348	8. **Push your changes** to your branch and open a merge request. The pre-publish checklist runs automatically and checks the metadata again. If it passes, the page is queued for review by the review cadence process.
349	
350	## Frequently Asked Questions
351	
352	**Q: Can I use a different date format, like MM/DD/YYYY?**  
353	A: No. The publishing system expects ISO 8601 format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) exclusively. Other formats cause validation to fail, and the page cannot be published.
354	
355	**Q: What if I fix just a typo or a single word? Do I have to bump the version?**  
356	A: Yes. Even a single-word fix should increment the patch version (e.g., `3.2.0` → `3.2.1`), update the last_updated date, and add a change log entry. This keeps the version timeline and changelog accurate and lets readers know the page has been reviewed and corrected.
357	
358	**Q: Can a page have multiple owners?**  
359	A: Yes. List them as `Team Name (Person A and Person B)`. Avoid more than two owners on a single page. If content is split across three or more teams, consider splitting the page itself or designating section owners instead.
360	
361	**Q: What if the page owner leaves the team or changes positions?**
362	A: Update the owner field immediately to the new owner's name and team. Add a note in the change log: "Ownership transferred to [new owner]." The publishing system uses the owner field to send review reminders and alerts, so this update is critical for keeping the review cadence on track.
363	
364	**Q: Is the "Applies to" field required?**  
365	A: No, it is optional. Use it if the page's content applies only to certain versions of oauthsvc or only to users with specific configurations. If the page applies to all versions and all users, omit the field.
366	
367	**Q: My page is very long and has three distinct sections owned by different people. Should I list all three in the owner field?**  
368	A: No. Instead, designate one person as the primary owner (in the owner field) and use section-level ownership notes within the page for the other sections. See the "Section Structure and Internal Ownership" section above for details.
369	
370	**Q: Can I include a change log entry for a change that happened before I created the page?**  
371	A: No. The change log should document changes to the page from the point of its creation forward. If the page is new, start with `v1.0.0` and a single entry describing its initial release.
372	
373	## Glossary
374	
375	**Changelog** – A section at the end of a page listing all updates in reverse chronological order (newest first), organized by version and date. Each entry summarizes the changes made in that version and optionally notes the oauthsvc release it was part of.
376	
377	**Draft** – A page stored in the repository branch that has not yet been published to the live docs site. Drafts are reviewed, validated, and queued before being moved to published status.
378	
379	**Field** – A labeled metadata value in the front-matter block at the top of a page, such as title, version, owner, or last_updated. Fields are structured data that the publishing system parses and validates.
380	
381	**Front-Matter** – The block of metadata at the very top of a page, before any content headings or body text. Front-matter is enclosed in delimiters (triple hyphens for YAML, or field list syntax for reStructuredText) and tells the publishing system about the page's title, version, owner, and other attributes.
382	
383	**Header Block** – A synonym for front-matter; the structured metadata section that precedes page content and carries authorship, versioning, and maintenance information.
384	
385	**Markdown** – A lightweight plain-text markup format used for most oauthsvc documentation pages. Markdown is human-readable in a text editor and easy to convert to HTML for web display.
386	
387	**Publishing Workflow** – The automated process that validates a page's metadata and content, sends it for review, and moves it to the live docs site once accepted. The workflow runs in stages: draft → review → queued → published.
388	
389	**reStructuredText** – A plain-text markup format more formal than Markdown, used for some oauthsvc documentation pages and often preferred for reference documentation and API references.
390	
391	**Semantic Versioning** – A versioning scheme where version numbers take the form major.minor.patch (e.g., 1.2.3). A patch bump signals a small fix or clarification; a minor bump signals new content or features; a major bump signals a breaking change or major restructuring.
392	
393	**Validation** – The automated process of checking that a page's metadata is complete, correctly formatted, and consistent with other pages and version records. Validation fails if required fields are missing, dates are malformed, version numbers are not incremented, or owner names are not recognized.
394

# Page Metadata Fields

**Title:** Page Metadata Fields  
**Version:** v1.2.0  
**Owner:** Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)  
**Last Updated:** 2025-04-28

## Summary

This page enumerates the front-matter fields that every oauthsvc documentation page must carry for the publishing tooling. All documentation pages, regardless of markup format, follow a common metadata structure to ensure consistency across the docs-style folder and enable automated publishing workflows. This page describes required fields, optional fields, validation rules, syntax for different formats, and how the documentation program processes metadata during review and publication.

## Overview of the Metadata System

Every documentation page in the oauthsvc repository carries a header block containing structured metadata. The publishing system reads these fields to organize the docs site, verify page authorship and currency, flag pages due for review, and generate site navigation. Pages are written in Markdown, reStructuredText, or plain text, but all carry equivalent metadata sections at the top.

The metadata structure serves several purposes:

- **Publishing:** The automated workflow uses metadata to generate site navigation, breadcrumb links, version indicators, and last-updated badges on the published docs site.
- **Review:** The review cadence process consults last_updated dates to flag pages that exceed their scheduled review interval.
- **Discoverability:** Page metadata enables search filters by owner, topic, and recency; team members query the metadata store to identify pages that need ownership updates or orphaned docs.
- **Accountability:** The owner field establishes who is responsible for keeping content accurate; this becomes critical when team members transition positions or leave.

Metadata validation runs automatically during the pre-publish checklist and again when pages enter the publishing queue. Pages that fail validation cannot be published.

## Metadata Field Definitions

All documentation pages must include these required fields in the header block at the very top, before any content:

### Title
The human-readable page title that appears in browser tabs, site navigation, and as the page heading. Titles should be concise (ideally 3–7 words) and match the page's primary topic. Titles must be fewer than 50 characters and must not include colons (which conflict with YAML parsing) or special characters except hyphens and parentheses.

**Valid examples:** `Page Metadata Fields`, `Voice and Tone Guidelines`, `How to Update the Glossary`

**Invalid examples:** `Page Metadata Fields: A Complete Guide` (contains colon), `oauthsvc @Docs` (contains invalid character)

### Version
The semantic version identifier for the page itself, distinct from the oauthsvc package version. Versions follow the format `major.minor.patch`, optionally prefixed with `v`. Both `1.2.0` and `v1.2.0` are valid; the publishing system normalizes them to the same canonical form.

Version bumps are semantic:
- **Patch (1.2.0 → 1.2.1):** Fix typos, clarify existing content, reword sentences without changing meaning or breadth.
- **Minor (1.2.0 → 1.3.0):** Add new sections, procedures, worked examples, or tables; expand existing sections; reorganize content structure.
- **Major (1.2.0 → 2.0.0):** Substantially restructure the page, remove major sections, or fundamentally change the page's breadth or audience.

Every version bump must be accompanied by an update to the last_updated date and a new entry in the change log. The publishing system will reject a commit that changes the version field without updating last_updated.

**Valid examples:** `v1.2.0`, `2.4`, `1.0.1`, `3.5.2`

### Owner
The person or team responsible for keeping the page accurate, current, and aligned with oauthsvc development. Use the format `Team Name (Person's Name)` for clarity, or just the team name if ownership is distributed. The owner is the primary point of contact for review questions, merge requests, and update schedules.

When multiple people share ownership of a single page, list them as: `Team Name (Person A and Person B)`. Avoid assigning more than two people to a page; if content is split across multiple owners, consider splitting the page itself.

**Valid examples:** `Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)`, `Developer Experience`, `Docs Guild (Nadia Reyes and Priya Chandran)`

### Last Updated
The ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD format) when the page content was last modified, added to, or corrected. This field is updated whenever any content changes, not only when the version number is incremented. The publishing system uses this date to calculate whether a page is overdue for review per the documentation review cadence.

Dates must not be in the future. The publishing system rejects any last_updated value later than the current date.

**Valid examples:** `2025-04-28`, `2026-06-10`, `2024-12-05`

**Invalid examples:** `2026-09-28` (if today is 2026-09-27), `04/28/2025` (wrong format), `April 28, 2025` (not ISO 8601)

### Optional Fields

These fields are optional but strongly recommended:

- **Reviewed by:** Name and date of the most recent substantive review (separate from content edits). Format: `Person Name (YYYY-MM-DD)`. Example: `Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)`. This field helps distinguish between a page that was simply updated and one that was fully reviewed for accuracy.
- **Applies to:** Version range or release identifier for the content's applicability. Examples: `oauthsvc 1.5+`, `all versions`, `1.4 and later`. Use this field if the documentation is version-specific or deprecated for older releases.

## Front-Matter Syntax by Format

### Markdown (.md) Pages

Markdown pages use YAML front-matter enclosed in triple hyphens at the very top of the file, before any content:

```
---
title: Page Metadata Fields
version: v1.2.0
owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
last_updated: 2025-04-28
reviewed_by: Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)
---

# Page Metadata Fields

## Overview
Content begins here.
```

Note that YAML field names use underscores (`last_updated`) rather than spaces. The `---` markers must appear on their own lines.

### reStructuredText (.rst) Pages

reStructuredText pages use field list syntax at the top of the file before any section headings:

```
:Title: Page Metadata Fields
:Version: v1.2.0
:Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
:Last Updated: 2025-04-28
:Reviewed By: Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)

Page Metadata Fields
====================

Overview
--------
Content begins here.
```

The field names use spaces and title case. There are no blank lines between field list items.

### Plain Text (.txt) Pages

Plain text pages include a brief header block in key-value format before the first blank line:

```
Title: Page Metadata Fields
Version: v1.2.0
Owner: Platform Tools (Mara Olsen)
Last Updated: 2025-04-28
Reviewed By: Ilse Vogel (2025-04-15)

# Page Metadata Fields

## Overview
Content begins here.
```

## Metadata Validation Rules

The publishing system validates metadata before a page can enter the docs site. Validation occurs during the pre-publish checklist run and again when the page is queued for deployment. If validation fails at either stage, the publishing workflow halts and alerts the page owner.

| Field | Required | Validation Rule |
|-------|----------|-----------------|
| title | Yes | 3–50 characters; must not contain colons; only hyphens and parentheses allowed as special chars |
| version | Yes | Semantic version format (major.minor.patch); must differ from the previous version in the changelog |
| owner | Yes | Must match an active team or person name on the docs team roster |
| last_updated | Yes | ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD); must not be a future date; must be different from previous date in changelog |
| reviewed_by | No | If present, must include person name and ISO 8601 date |
| applies_to | No | Free text; no format validation |

Common validation failures and their causes:

- **Invalid date format:** The system expects `YYYY-MM-DD`. Formats like `04-28-2025`, `2025/04/28`, or `April 28, 2025` cause immediate rejection.
- **Title contains colon:** YAML parsing fails if the title includes a `:` character. Use em dashes or parentheses instead.
- **Missing required field:** A page without a title, version, owner, or last_updated cannot be published. The validator names the missing field.
- **Version not incremented:** If the page content has changed but the version matches the previous version, validation fails. Update the patch, minor, or major version accordingly.
- **Owner not recognized:** The owner name must match a current team or individual in the docs team roster, maintained separately. If an owner has departed, update this field before publishing.
- **Stale page:** If last_updated is more than 180 days old, the page is flagged by the review cadence checker and queued for review, but it is not blocked from publishing. A stale page can still be published if its content is accurate; the flag prompts a review cycle.

To verify metadata validation locally before committing, run the validation script:

```
./scripts/validate-metadata.sh docs-style/writing-style-guide.md
```

If validation passes, the script produces no output. If there are errors, it prints them to your terminal, one per line:

```
ERROR: title contains invalid character ':' at position 45
ERROR: last_updated date is in the future (2026-09-28 > 2026-09-27)
```

## Section Structure and Internal Ownership

Beyond the page-level metadata, pages should organize their content with section headings in logical order. For pages longer than 2,000 words or with content split across multiple teams, consider assigning a section owner—a person responsible for accuracy and currency of that specific section.

Section ownership is optional but recommended when:
- A page covers multiple topics maintained by different teams.
- A section is highly technical and benefits from specialized expertise.
- Multiple people contribute to a single page but own distinct portions.

To indicate section ownership, add a note immediately after the section heading:

**Example:**

```
## Configuration Files
*Section owner: Priya Chandran*

These files control...
```

A section owner is consulted during review cycles for that section only. If a section owner departs, update the note to reflect the new owner and mention the change in the page's change log.

## Glossary and Terminology Requirements

Every documentation page must include a terminology section (titled "Glossary," "Terminology," "Terms," or similar) that defines at least eight terms used in that page. These page-specific terms supplement the central oauthsvc glossary and may differ from it. When a term is defined in both places, readers should understand that the page glossary takes precedence on that page.

Glossary entries should be:
- In alphabetical order.
- One to three sentences long; avoid circular definitions.
- Specific to the page's content and audience.
- Formatted consistently (bullet list, definition list, or table).

**Example glossary entry:**

```
### Loopback Server
The lightweight HTTP service bundled with the package that maintains state and serves configuration data. It runs locally on the system and uses the SQLite database file for persistence.
```

**Do not:**
- Define terms that appear nowhere in the page (filling out the list).
- Cross-reference the central glossary instead of providing your own definition.
- Use undefined jargon within a glossary definition.
- List more than fifteen terms (if you need more, the page is too broad; consider splitting it).

If a term used in your page is already defined in the central oauthsvc Glossary (version v3.0.1, maintained by Developer Experience), you may omit it from your page glossary and instead note in that section: "See the oauthsvc Glossary for definitions of loopback server, database file, and other package-specific terms." However, do not omit terms; your page glossary must have at least eight entries.

## File and Path Listings

Every page must include a section (typically titled "References and Related Files" or "Repository Files") that lists repository files, configuration files, log folders, and other file system paths mentioned in the page. This section helps readers locate resources and understand the repository structure.

The listing should use a table or definition list format. For tables, include columns for path and function:

| Path | Function |
|------|------|
| `docs/` | Root folder for all user-facing documentation pages |
| `docs-style/` | Folder for internal documentation about the documentation program |
| `docs-style/metadata-fields.md` | This page; defines metadata schema for all pages |
| `docs-style/writing-style-guide.md` | House style rules for tone, voice, list formatting, and code snippets |
| `docs-style/glossary.md` | Centralized glossary of oauthsvc-specific terminology shared across all pages |
| `.publishing/queue.json` | Publishing workflow queue; read and written by the pub script |
| `scripts/validate-metadata.sh` | Command-line tool for validating page metadata before commit |

All paths are relative to the repository root. Prefix internal documentation paths with `docs-style/` and user-facing pages with `docs/`. Use backticks around file paths in tables and inline text.

Do not list files that are mentioned only in passing or used internally by oauthsvc. This section should cover files that readers might need to open, edit, or understand as context for the page.

## Tools and Package Versions

Pages that describe tools, external packages, dependencies, or other software should include a table (typically titled "Tools and Versions" or "External Dependencies") listing each tool with its version. Update this table whenever a dependency is upgraded or when oauthsvc's minimum version requirement changes.

| Tool | Version | Notes |
|------|---------|-------|
| Python | 3.10+ | Required for the package runtime and CLI |
| sqlite3 | 3.31+ | Standard library module included with Python; used for the database file |
| git | 2.30+ | Required for version control and repository operations |

The "Notes" column is optional but helpful for explaining version constraints, usage context, or why a version threshold is required.

If the page describes oauthsvc itself, do not include it in the tools table; assume readers know which version of oauthsvc they are using from the broader documentation context.

## Change Log

Every page must include a change log documenting updates to the page, organized by version and date. The change log must contain at least six entries. Entries are listed in reverse chronological order (newest first), one entry per version.

Each entry includes:
- The version number (matching the version field at that point in time).
- The date in ISO 8601 format.
- The oauthsvc release this page update was part of (optional but recommended).
- A bulleted list of changes (at least one bullet per entry).

**Format:**

```
## Change Log

### v1.2.0 (2025-04-28) – oauthsvc 1.5.0
- Added optional "Reviewed by" field for tracking review dates separately from content updates.
- Clarified that title field must not include colons or other special characters.
- Expanded section on section ownership for long-form documentation.
- Updated all examples to match current template versions.

### v1.1.2 (2025-02-14) – oauthsvc 1.4.3
- Fixed syntax error in reStructuredText field list example.
- Added note clarifying that version prefix (v vs. no prefix) is normalized by the publishing system.

### v1.1.1 (2025-01-30) – oauthsvc 1.4.2
- Corrected common misconception that page version is tied to package version; they are independent.

### v1.1.0 (2024-12-10) – oauthsvc 1.4.0
- Added plain-text (.txt) format for front-matter metadata.
- Expanded validation rules table with four new rules and examples of common failures.
- Introduced Frequently Asked Questions section.

### v1.0.2 (2024-10-15) – oauthsvc 1.3.1
- Corrected multiple date format examples from MM-DD-YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD.

### v1.0.1 (2024-09-05) – oauthsvc 1.3.0
- Minor clarifications to field definitions and syntax examples.
```

When you update a page, always:
1. Add a new entry at the top of the change log.
2. Increment the version number in the header.
3. Update the last_updated date.

The publishing system uses the change log to detect if version and last_updated have been changed consistently; mismatches trigger validation warnings.

## Related Pages

Pages in the docs-style folder are interconnected. Review these related pages to understand the broader documentation program and how metadata fits into it:

- **docs-style Folder Overview** (v1.4, Docs Guild) – Navigation and overview of all documentation program pages.
- **Writing Style Guide** (v3.2, Docs Guild) – House rules for tone, capitalization, list formatting, and handling code examples.
- **Voice and Tone Guidelines** (v2.0, Developer Experience) – Guidelines for the voice and tone that oauthsvc documentation should use.
- **Page Templates Overview** (v1.6.0, Platform Tools) – Layout patterns, boilerplate sections, and templates for different page types.
- **Template Field Reference** (v2.1, Platform Tools) – Detailed field-by-field reference for page templates; complements this page.
- **oauthsvc Glossary** (v3.0.1, Developer Experience) – Centralized glossary of oauthsvc-specific terminology used across all documentation.
- **Glossary Upkeep Process** (v1.3, Developer Experience) – Procedures for adding, updating, and deprecating terms in the central glossary.
- **Documentation Review Cadence** (v2.4, Platform Tools) – Schedule and criteria for reviewing pages based on last_updated date and content type.
- **Docs Publishing Workflow** (v2.2.0, Docs Guild) – How pages move from draft status through review to published status on the docs site.
- **Page Review Checklist** (v1.1, Platform Tools) – Checklist that reviewers use to verify page quality, accuracy, and metadata.
- **Pre-Publish Checklist** (v1.0, Docs Guild) – Automated checks that run before a page can be queued for deployment.
- **Markup Conventions** (v2.5, Developer Experience) – Conventions for code blocks, inline formatting, tables, and lists across all formats.

## Worked Example: Updating Metadata

Suppose you are updating the Writing Style Guide to add a new section on list formatting conventions. Here is the step-by-step process:

1. **Open the page** in your editor. Check the header block at the very top for current metadata.

2. **Find the current version.** The page header shows `version: 3.2`. Since you are adding a new section, increment the minor version: change to `version: 3.3`.

3. **Update the last_updated date** to today's date. If today is September 27, 2026, change the field to `last_updated: 2026-09-27`.

4. **Do not update the owner field** unless ownership has genuinely changed. The Writing Style Guide is owned by Docs Guild (Priya Chandran); leave it as is.

5. **Add a new entry at the top of the change log** section:

   ```
   ### v3.3 (2026-09-27) – oauthsvc 1.6.0
   - Added new section "List Formatting Conventions" covering nested bullet and numbered lists.
   - Clarified rules for indentation and spacing in mixed-list scenarios.
   - Added worked examples showing correct and incorrect list structures.
   ```

6. **Commit your changes** to the repository:

   ```
   git add docs-style/writing-style-guide.md
   git commit -m "docs: add list formatting conventions; bump to v3.3"
   ```

7. **Before pushing, run the metadata validator** locally:

   ```
   ./scripts/validate-metadata.sh docs-style/writing-style-guide.md
   ```

   If validation passes, no output is shown. If there are errors, the script prints them to your terminal and you can fix them before pushing.

8. **Push your changes** to your branch and open a merge request. The pre-publish checklist runs automatically and checks the metadata again. If it passes, the page is queued for review by the review cadence process.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can I use a different date format, like MM/DD/YYYY?**  
A: No. The publishing system expects ISO 8601 format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) exclusively. Other formats cause validation to fail, and the page cannot be published.

**Q: What if I fix just a typo or a single word? Do I have to bump the version?**  
A: Yes. Even a single-word fix should increment the patch version (e.g., `3.2.0` → `3.2.1`), update the last_updated date, and add a change log entry. This keeps the version timeline and changelog accurate and lets readers know the page has been reviewed and corrected.

**Q: Can a page have multiple owners?**  
A: Yes. List them as `Team Name (Person A and Person B)`. Avoid more than two owners on a single page. If content is split across three or more teams, consider splitting the page itself or designating section owners instead.

**Q: What if the page owner leaves the team or changes positions?**
A: Update the owner field immediately to the new owner's name and team. Add a note in the change log: "Ownership transferred to [new owner]." The publishing system uses the owner field to send review reminders and alerts, so this update is critical for keeping the review cadence on track.

**Q: Is the "Applies to" field required?**  
A: No, it is optional. Use it if the page's content applies only to certain versions of oauthsvc or only to users with specific configurations. If the page applies to all versions and all users, omit the field.

**Q: My page is very long and has three distinct sections owned by different people. Should I list all three in the owner field?**  
A: No. Instead, designate one person as the primary owner (in the owner field) and use section-level ownership notes within the page for the other sections. See the "Section Structure and Internal Ownership" section above for details.

**Q: Can I include a change log entry for a change that happened before I created the page?**  
A: No. The change log should document changes to the page from the point of its creation forward. If the page is new, start with `v1.0.0` and a single entry describing its initial release.

## Glossary

**Changelog** – A section at the end of a page listing all updates in reverse chronological order (newest first), organized by version and date. Each entry summarizes the changes made in that version and optionally notes the oauthsvc release it was part of.

**Draft** – A page stored in the repository branch that has not yet been published to the live docs site. Drafts are reviewed, validated, and queued before being moved to published status.

**Field** – A labeled metadata value in the front-matter block at the top of a page, such as title, version, owner, or last_updated. Fields are structured data that the publishing system parses and validates.

**Front-Matter** – The block of metadata at the very top of a page, before any content headings or body text. Front-matter is enclosed in delimiters (triple hyphens for YAML, or field list syntax for reStructuredText) and tells the publishing system about the page's title, version, owner, and other attributes.

**Header Block** – A synonym for front-matter; the structured metadata section that precedes page content and carries authorship, versioning, and maintenance information.

**Markdown** – A lightweight plain-text markup format used for most oauthsvc documentation pages. Markdown is human-readable in a text editor and easy to convert to HTML for web display.

**Publishing Workflow** – The automated process that validates a page's metadata and content, sends it for review, and moves it to the live docs site once accepted. The workflow runs in stages: draft → review → queued → published.

**reStructuredText** – A plain-text markup format more formal than Markdown, used for some oauthsvc documentation pages and often preferred for reference documentation and API references.

**Semantic Versioning** – A versioning scheme where version numbers take the form major.minor.patch (e.g., 1.2.3). A patch bump signals a small fix or clarification; a minor bump signals new content or features; a major bump signals a breaking change or major restructuring.

**Validation** – The automated process of checking that a page's metadata is complete, correctly formatted, and consistent with other pages and version records. Validation fails if required fields are missing, dates are malformed, version numbers are not incremented, or owner names are not recognized.

## References and Related Files

- `docs/` – Root directory containing all user-facing documentation pages.
- `docs-style/README.md` – Overview and navigation guide for the docs-style internal documentation folder.
- `docs-style/writing-style-guide.md` – House style and tone guidelines for all pages; referenced by reviewers.
- `docs-style/page-templates.md` – Template layouts and boilerplate sections for common page types.
- `docs-style/glossary.md` – Central glossary of oauthsvc-specific terminology; shared across all pages.
- `docs-style/glossary-upkeep.md` – Process for maintaining and updating the central glossary.
- `docs-style/review-cadence.md` – Review schedule and criteria based on last_updated dates.
- `docs-style/publishing-workflow.md` – Publishing process and stages from draft to live site.
- `docs-style/review-checklist.txt` – Checklist used by reviewers to validate page quality.
- `docs-style/publishing-checklist.txt` – Pre-publication checks run by automated tooling.
- `.publishing/queue.json` – Publishing queue file; read and updated by the pub automation script.
- `scripts/validate-metadata.sh` – Command-line tool for validating page metadata before commit.

## Change Log

### v1.2.0 (2025-04-28) – oauthsvc 1.5.0
- Added optional "Reviewed by" field for tracking review dates separately from content update dates.
- Clarified that title field must not include colons and specified title character limits.
- Expanded section on section-level ownership for pages with distributed authorship.
- Added comprehensive Frequently Asked Questions section.
- Updated all examples throughout to reflect current template versions.
- Expanded the validation rules table with additional failure scenarios and error messages.

### v1.1.2 (2025-02-14) – oauthsvc 1.4.3
- Fixed syntax error in the reStructuredText field list example.
- Added clarifying note that version prefix (`v` vs. no prefix) is normalized by the publishing system.

### v1.1.1 (2025-01-30) – oauthsvc 1.4.2
- Corrected common misconception in the version field definition: page version is independent from package version.

### v1.1.0 (2024-12-10) – oauthsvc 1.4.0
- Added support for plain-text (.txt) format front-matter metadata.
- Expanded validation rules table from five rules to nine, with examples of common failures.
- Introduced Frequently Asked Questions section.
- Clarified section ownership notation for pages with distributed authorship.

### v1.0.2 (2024-10-15) – oauthsvc 1.3.1
- Corrected date format in multiple examples from MM-DD-YYYY to YYYY-MM-DD.

### v1.0.1 (2024-09-05) – oauthsvc 1.3.0
- Minor clarifications to field definitions and added additional syntax examples.

### v1.0.0 (2024-08-20) – oauthsvc 1.2.0
- Initial release of the metadata field standard.
- Defined required fields: title, version, owner, last_updated.
- Defined optional fields: reviewed_by, applies_to.
- Specified validation rules and front-matter syntax for Markdown, reStructuredText, and plain-text formats.
- Established change log requirements (minimum six entries).
- Documented glossary and terminology requirements (minimum eight terms per page).
